title: Verify a PIM Manager installation
purpose: Verifies a PIM Manager installation at the end of the install (and any time later): it reads every result an install must leave behind, repairs what can be repaired, prints one table with the fix for each line, and refuses "done" when a required line fails.
whenToRun: Every install path runs it as its last step. Run it yourself after a private installation (from inside the network: the store has no public endpoint), after an interrupted install, or whenever you want to know the installation is complete. It is part of the PIM Manager release package, not a separate download: run it from the package folder that Install-Invardia (or the guided install) downloaded and verified (.\tools\setup\Confirm-PimInstall.ps1). It reads over REST (browser sign-in or the Invardia Support app session; no Azure CLI).

runAs.name: Reader
runAs.scope: the PIM resource group (Contributor for the updater repair; Owner or User Access Administrator for the role repairs)
runAs.why: Reads the Manager app, the engine and updater jobs, their identities, role assignments and the SQL firewall rules. A repair (updater re-install, the Manager's Reader on the resource group, removing this run's 'AllowSetupHost' rule) needs the matching write right; without it the line stays failed or a warning, with its fix.

runAs.name: Member of the environment's SQL admin group (grp-pim-sql-admins), signed in through the browser or the Invardia Support app session (-UseSignedInAccount), or an admin application with a certificate (-ClientId + -CertThumbprint)
runAs.why: Reads ManagerAccess, the licence, the mail sender and the alert recipients from pim.Settings; the SuperAdmin and alert-recipient repairs write them (Set-PimManagerAccess / Set-PimAlertRecipients).

runAs.name: Global Reader (or any role that can read service principals and their application permission assignments)
runAs.why: Checks that the engine identity holds every required Microsoft Graph application permission (appRoleAssignments) and that every SuperAdmin may sign in to the Manager (Easy Auth assignments).

runAs.name: Global Administrator (only for the tenant-root Reader repair)
runAs.why: The one grant attempt of the engine's Reader at the tenant root. Without it the line is a warning carrying the Global Administrator's command; the install is still done. Missing Graph permissions are granted by a Privileged Role Administrator with Grant-PimEnginePermissions.ps1 (printed as the fix).

runAs.name: Exchange Administrator (optional)
runAs.why: Tests that each sending identity holds the scoped 'Application Mail.Send' right (Test-ServicePrincipalAuthorization). Without it the mail line is a warning; mail is optional.

changes.object: pim.Settings ManagerAccess (a named SuperAdmin missing) -- repair, via Set-PimManagerAccess
changes.why: Every SuperAdmin of the install must be a SuperAdmin in the Manager. Never written when the store could not be read.
changes.undo: Manager > Settings > Access: change the role back.

changes.object: pim.Settings alert recipients (empty) -- repair, via Set-PimAlertRecipients
changes.why: An install must not leave alerting without recipients.

changes.object: the updater job ca-pim-update (missing or wrong ring) -- repair, via Deploy-PimUpdateJob on the running image
changes.why: A Pro installation must keep itself updated.
changes.undo: Delete or change the updater job (its ring is PIM_UPDATE_RING).

changes.object: the engine job's managed identity -- one attempt
changes.why: So the engine sees every subscription. Refused = a warning with the command.
changes.undo: Remove the role assignment at the tenant root.

changes.object: the Manager's managed identity -- one attempt
changes.why: The Manager's Environment report reads its own resources.
changes.undo: Remove the role assignment on the resource group.

changes.object: the 'AllowSetupHost' rule this run opened (only with -CloseSetupHostRule and -SetupHostRuleOwner this)
changes.why: No setup-time firewall opening is left behind.
changes.undo: None needed (an install opens it again when it needs it).

changes.object: the result as JSON (done, failed, warnings, rows)
changes.why: For a caller that reads the outcome.

parameters.name: Role

parameters.name: AlertRecipients
parameters.help: The alert recipients to repair an empty list with.

parameters.help: The expected update ring (-1 = not checked).

parameters.name: UpdateSource
parameters.help: The update source of the updater repair (e.g. Invardia).

parameters.name: NoUpdater
parameters.help: A Community installation without a feed: there is no in-cloud updater by design (Update-PimCommunity.ps1 is its updater).

parameters.name: LicenceExpected
parameters.help: Pro, trial or multi-tenant: a registered licence is required.

parameters.name: MailDeferredReason
parameters.help: Why the install could not set the mail sender (the line is then a warning with the Get Started follow-up).

parameters.name: SetupHostRuleOwner
parameters.help: Who owns the 'AllowSetupHost' SQL firewall rule: this run, the caller (the multi-tenant build closes it in its last step) or none.

parameters.name: ClosingStep
parameters.help: The caller's step that closes the rule (shown in the line).

parameters.name: CloseSetupHostRule
parameters.help: Remove this run's 'AllowSetupHost' rule and read it back.

parameters.name: EngineAzureRootUserAccessAdmin
parameters.help: The root repair also grants the engine User Access Administrator (so it can assign Azure roles).

parameters.name: MasterSubscriptionId
parameters.help: Managed tenant: the managing tenant's subscription (for the lines it can read from here).

parameters.name: MasterStorageAccount
parameters.help: Managed tenant: the managing tenant's bundle store.

parameters.name: ManagingTenantStep
parameters.help: Managed tenant: the managing tenant's step shown when a line cannot be read from here.

parameters.name: ResumeCommand
parameters.help: The command that re-runs this install's verify (shown as the fix of a repairable line).

parameters.name: ClientId
parameters.help: Automation: an admin application's client id (with -CertThumbprint) instead of the signed-in account.

parameters.name: CertThumbprint
parameters.help: Automation: that application's certificate thumbprint (local machine store).

parameters.name: UseSignedInAccount
parameters.help: Read (and repair) as the signed-in person: the recommended way.

parameters.name: NoRepair
parameters.help: Read and report only; no repair runs.

parameters.name: OutFile
parameters.help: Write the result as JSON to this file.

readsOnly: pim.Settings: ManagerAccess, License, the install key state, the mail sender, the alert recipients
the Manager app, the engine / updater / downlink jobs and their executions, their identities and role assignments (management.azure.com)
the engine identity's Microsoft Graph application permissions (appRoleAssignments) and the Manager's sign-in app assignments
Exchange Online Test-ServicePrincipalAuthorization for each sending identity (when Exchange is reachable)
the SQL server's firewall rules; managed tenant: the managing tenant's store network rules
whatIf: Reads every line and prints the table with each fix; every repair it would make is previewed as 'What if: Performing the operation "repair" on target "install check '<line>'"' and not run, so a repairable line keeps its failed state. Nothing is written.
undo: Nothing to undo for the check itself. A repair is undone the way its line says: the SuperAdmin / alert recipients in the Manager's Settings, the updater job, the two Reader role assignments.
